problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis. When the displacement of $P$ from the origin $O$ is $x$ meters, its velocity is $v\,\text{m/s}$ and its acceleration is ${e}^{-2x}\,{m/s}^{2}.$ Which differential equation describes this motion?
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14041958/assets/dd924518ae28ee8bf010e76b95ddbd68a26137b8b1f28753900455a87e1df799.png)

Since the acceleration of the particle $P$ is ${e}^{-2x}\,{m/s}^{2},$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}={e}^{-2x}.
$$

Using the chain rule for differentiation, we can rewrite this equation as

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}={e}^{-2x}.
$$

Now, since $v=\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},$ we obtain the differential equation

$$
v\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{-2x}.
$$
